title: When a genealogical determination is admissible

statements.text: A genealogical determination is admissible only if it states its projection, speaks from the object's own state space, names an invariant available from inside it, explains why structural-functional derivation cannot reach it, and contradicts nothing already established about the object.

sources.quote: A genealogical determination is admissible if and only if it satisfies five conditions.
No known zero of the zeta function contradicts the critical-line determination.
